title: Plan: the page system
description: The class architecture, short and current; every change traces back here.

add.text: Four classes, each one builds on the last

add.title: Item → List → Page → LivePage
add.text:
```
Item       one saved node, no DOM          core/Item/Item.js
 └ List    an ordered set of Items          core/List/List.js
Item
 └ Page    an Item with a url and a folder   core/Page/Page.class.js
    └ LivePage  a Page drawn by small views  live/LivePage.js
```
- **Item**: holds data, saves itself as lines, replays them.
- **List**: `page.content` is one; add, remove, move.
- **Page**: one url, one folder, one `page.jsonl`, children are sub-pages.
- **LivePage**: draws through `Head`, `Crumbs`, `Main`, `Card`, `Block`, `Children`, `Foot`; replace one to change one part.
Where the data lives: three shapes

add.title: Embedded, own folder, or Ref
add.text:
```
public/live/design/
  page.jsonl        ← the page, and every card in it (embedded)
  storage/
    page.jsonl      ← a sub-page: its own folder (own folder)
{"type":"ref","to":"/live/lab/"}   ← points at an Item in another file (Ref)
```
- **Embedded**: a card is a line in its page's file. The default.
- **Own folder**: a sub-page gets a folder and its own `page.jsonl`.
- **Ref**: a pointer; it follows `moved_to` when the target moves.
- **When does a card get a folder?** Proposed, not built: when it needs a file beside it or a sub-page. It moves with `Item.move_to({url})` and leaves a Ref. [The proposal](/framework/core/Page/doc/recursive-pages.md)
Urls: the folder is the address

tsyquen2.text:
```
public/live/design/
  page.jsonl        ← the page, and every card in it (embedded)
  storage/
    page.jsonl      ← a sub-page: its own folder (own folder)
{"type":"Ref","url":"/live/lab/","path":"content.k2"}   ← a pointer (Ref)
```
- **Embedded**: a card is a line in its page's file. The default.
- **Own folder**: a sub-page gets a folder and its own `page.jsonl`.
- **Ref**: points at an Item in this file or another (`core/Item/Ref.js`); it follows `moved_to` when the target moves, and shows "gone" when nothing is there.
- **When does a card get a folder?** Proposed, not built: when it needs a file beside it or a sub-page. It moves with `Item.move_to({url})` and leaves a Ref. [The proposal](/framework/core/Page/doc/recursive-pages.md)

add.title: Url = folder; tabs = sub-pages; crumbs = the url
add.text:
```
/live/design/storage/   →  public/live/design/storage/page.jsonl

Live › design › storage   ← the breadcrumb is location.pathname, split
[ Today | Pages | Storage ]  ← each tab is a child page with its own url
```
- **Routes**: the Router walks a page's children; a folder with `page.jsonl` is a page.
- **Tabs**: a page with `navigation: "tabs"` shows its children as tabs. Clicking one goes to that child's url.
- **Breadcrumbs**: exactly the parts of `location.pathname`, each a link. Being checked on plain-Page tabs ([tabs page](/live/demos/tabs-page/)).
- **Loading**: a page loads its children's files 2 levels deep, each file in full. A wide folder costs the most; small preview files (`index.jsonl`) are the planned fix. [The numbers](/framework/core/Page/doc/recursive-pages.md)
Reading and changing a page

add.title: The item tool: one read, one write
add.text:
```js
item({ path: "/live/plan/", read: "content" })              // read, never writes
item({ path: "/live/plan/", delta: { title: "Plan" } })     // a plain key: set it
item({ path, delta: { content: { add: { type: "part-card" } } } })  // a method key: call it
item({ path, delta: { k2: { text: "new" } } })              // a card id: walk into it
```
- **Every write is one line** appended to the page's `page.jsonl`; every open tab redraws.
- **Bug, fix queued**: a delta the page refuses (a card id like `pages`) is still appended. The fix checks first, then appends; it goes live at the next Servex restart.

add.title: Settings: a page's own controls
add.text:
- **/settings/** under a live page: its class, its file and its layout words. Being built on the live page (sticky header with a tab row), in review.
- **Coming next to it**: an inspector for any page or card (its class, where it is stored, its children, the methods you can call, and its change history with a replay slider).
Decisions: what changed, and why

add.title: Decision log (newest first)
add.text:
| Old | New | Why |
|---|---|---|
| A namespace refactor of Page | **Not started** | Asked to hold it; the classes above stay as they are |
| Every child file loaded in full | Small preview files (`index.jsonl`), **planned** | A wide folder is the cost; a deep one is bounded |
| A card gets a folder by hand | Promote when it needs a file or a sub-page, **proposed** | One rule; the old place keeps a Ref |
| Columns only on a live page | **Works on a plain Page** | Same layout word everywhere |
| A Files chip per page | **One Files button** in the title row of a jsonl page | One way to open a page's file |
| Design page redrew cards itself | **Extends `LivePage.Card` and `Block`** | One drawing seam; a fix to the live page reaches it |

Alternatives for each: [recursive-pages.md](/framework/core/Page/doc/recursive-pages.md) · [jsonl.md](/framework/core/Page/doc/jsonl.md) · [design page](/live/design/)
The owner's view: keep what works, cut the rest

add.title: Keep: these work well
add.text:
- **The breadcrumb.** It gets deeper as you drill into settings, and you can climb back up it.
- **The gear.** It opens the settings page.
- **Browsing the files from the site**, including the code view at `/settings/<file>/`.

All three should move into the default `Page` class one day. The core class doc pages (such as `/framework/core/Page/`) would move onto this system too. *Migration candidate: analyse it first.*

add.title: Too complicated: what to simplify
add.text:
- **Too many page-only classes.** `LiveButton`, `LiveLight`, `LiveChecklist`, `LiveScreen` and `LiveContent` should be generic parts (Checklist, Button, Light) that turn live only when a page needs them.
- **`core/Page/parts/`, and loose lowercase files like `parts/kinds.js`.** Nobody can say what a "part" is: a view? A template? And a lowercase module is not a class.
- **About 13 import lines in `LivePage.js`.** One entry file (`core/core.js`) could export everything, so each page needs fewer lines.
- **Imports nobody can explain**, such as `ux/content/Object` and its `DefaultView`. Each one gets a one-line reason.
- **The goal.** `Page` is the root class for templates. Every reusable piece gets its own page, which draws it, holds its variants and fits it into one design system. There is one library of parts, imported anywhere.

add.title: Icons and tabs
add.text:
- **Icons.** Every page can name its own icon. It shows in the header where the status dot is now, and the dot can sit beside it. A folder gets a folder icon, and settings gets a gear.
- **Tabs.** Tabs are a few permanent sections with short names (Live, Log, Settings). A post such as "Plan: the page system" is not a tab.

add.title: Later: audit the old systems
add.text: Old systems such as `/live/sessions/` (from v1) and `/live/next/` need an audit: what each one is for, and when it was last used. This is logged here and not started yet.

add.title: The simplification plan: analysis running
add.text: A read-only pass is listing every `Live*` class, every file in `parts/` and every import, with what each is for. The proposal will replace this card. Nothing is refactored until the proposal is approved.

ov-plan.title: The simplification plan: six steps, smallest first
ov-plan.text:
Nothing has been changed yet. Each step is one small merge, and the ones near the top are cheapest and safest.

1. **Move `TaskState.js` out of /live/** into `core/Task/`. It has nothing to do with /live/ and has one caller. *About 15 min, no risk.*
2. **Delete the old alias files in `core/Page/parts/`**: `Part.js`, `Parts.js`, `HeadingPart.js`, `TextPart.js` and `CardPart.js`, which only keep old names alive. A part is just an Item with its own View, drawn in a page's content list. Search the repo for the old names first. *About 30 min, low risk.*
3. **Add one entry file, `core/core.js`**, exporting Page, View and its tags, Item, List, PageLink and the part types. LivePage's seven framework import lines become one. *About 20 min, no risk.*
4. **Turn the Live\* cards into generic parts:** LiveButton, LiveLight and LiveChecklist become `part-button`, `part-light` and `part-checklist` in `core/Page/parts/`. The old `live-*` names stay as aliases, so saved pages still load. LiveScreen and LiveContent stay in /live/, because saving screens and keeping removed cards are /live/'s own features. *1 to 1.5 h, medium risk; check /live/ afterwards.*
5. **Move the settings file browser and its `/settings/<file>/` code view onto the default Page.** It depends on nothing that only /live/ has. *About 1 h, low risk.*
6. **Give the default Page an optional header** with the breadcrumb, gear, settings page and the page's icon. A page turns it on with one field, so no existing page changes until it opts in. `/framework/core/Page/` is the first to use it. *2 to 3 h.*

**Icons:** pages can already declare an icon (`Page.fields`), but nothing draws it in the header yet. The next /live/ update adds it there, next to the status dot.

**Imports you asked about:** `DefaultView` (`ux/Content/Object/DefaultView.js`) is the site's shared helper that redraws only the items in a list that changed. Many pages use it; it is not specific to /live/.

**Audit (logged, not started):** /live/sessions/ is still a live page that reads the old v1 log. /live/next/ does not exist, so that name was probably meant to be /live/v1/ or /live/archive/.

Full analysis, with file and line for each claim: [analysis.md](/framework/ai/sessions/2026/11/06/spawned/mastermind-page-design/simplify/analysis.md)

add.title: Type names become class names
add.text:
A card's `type` will be its exact class name, so the name on a page line matches the code: `LiveCode`, not `live-code`. The new `View` type already works this way.

- **What changes:** each `Item.register(LiveCode, "live-code")` becomes `Item.register(LiveCode)`, which already defaults to the class name. The old name stays as an alias that only reads, so old logs still replay. New lines are written with the class name.
- **Which ones:** `live-light`, `live-button`, `live-checklist`, `live-code` and `live-screen`, plus the six `part-*` types (`part-card` becomes `PageCard`, and so on).
- **Order:** it goes with step 4 (generic cards), since those classes are renamed in the same move. *About 1 h, plus a replay check of every saved /live/ page.*

add.title: page.items: where each item is saved

add.text: Open questions: items, routes and ids (not built yet)

add.title: 1. A thing is an Item that can have a page
add.text:
Page = Item + a route (+ sub-routes it makes itself). A player or a user should not *be* a Page: Page's namespace is too big.

- **A. Everything extends Page (today).** ➕ the route comes free. ➖ every player carries a hundred page methods, and a field can clash with one (`render`).
- **B. Any Item can be opened as a page.** The route reaches the item, then a page is drawn around it (`item.page()` on demand). ➕ Items stay small, and one rule covers every item. ➖ the Page class must accept an item to show, so it needs care (we are not refactoring Page's names now).
- **C. A route plugin** (`Player.use(Routable)`, core/Plugin). ➕ opt-in. ➖ two ways to be a page: by class, or by plugin.

**Leaning B**, built in steps: the Page class stays, and any Item a url reaches opens inside a page.

add.title: 2. One url reaches any item
add.text:
One scheme for a solo view of any item, wherever it is saved: a line in page.jsonl, its own file, or its own folder.

```
/live/item-test/thing
// folder thing/?  open it
// else thing.jsonl?  open it
// else an item with id thing
```

- **A. Short url, fixed search order:** a folder first, then a file, then the page's lists (`items`, `content`). ➕ short and readable. ➖ two lists holding the same id: the first one wins.
- **B. The list is in the url:** `/live/item-test/items/thing`, mirroring `page.items.thing`. ➕ never ambiguous. ➖ longer, and a list name sits in every url.
- **C. A hash for embedded items:** `/live/item-test/#thing`. ➕ needs no route at all. ➖ not a page of its own, and different from file items.

**Leaning A**, with B always accepted as the long form.

add.title: 3. A trailing slash means "draw it"
add.text:
Today there are three patterns: `/settings/LivePage.js/` (code drawn as a page), `/md/...` (markdown drawn), and possibly `/x/thing.jsonl/`.

```
/x/readme.md     the raw file
/x/readme.md/    drawn as a page
/x/thing.jsonl/  the item, drawn
```

- **A. One rule: a file name + slash = its drawn view.** ➕ one rule for every file type, and the raw file keeps its own url (static hosting still works). ➖ the `/settings/` and `/md/` urls change, so the old ones need redirects.
- **B. A prefix per viewer** (`/md/`, `/settings/`, `/code/`). ➕ says which viewer. ➖ one more prefix per file type: today's mess.
- **C. A query** (`?view`, `?raw`). ➕ nothing new to route. ➖ ugly to share and to read on a phone.

**Leaning A**, with the old urls redirected.

add.title: 4. Ids use _, urls use -
add.text:
In JS an id should read `page.some_thing`; in a url, `some-thing` looks right.

- **A. Map them: `_` in the id, `-` in the url.** The router reads both spellings. ➕ each place looks native. ➖ an id that already has a `-` can't come back out: so ids never contain `-` (the id is cleaned when it is made).
- **B. Underscores everywhere**, urls included. ➕ nothing to map. ➖ the url looks odd, and a link's underline hides `_`.
- **C. Hyphens everywhere**, so JS writes `page.get("some-thing")`. ➕ one spelling. ➖ no `page.some_thing` dot access.

**Leaning A.**

add.title: 5. Where an id comes from, and spaces
add.text:
The order, first match wins: the id you pass, else the file name (`thing.jsonl` → `thing`), else the title, else a random one. The build in progress already uses the file name.

A title has spaces ("My Thing"). Three ways to turn it into an id:

- **A. Clean it:** `my_thing` (lowercase, a space becomes `_`), url `my-thing`. Taken? `my_thing_2`. ➕ clean ids and urls; the id stays put when the title changes. ➖ the id no longer reads exactly like the title.
- **B. Keep the spaces:** id `My Thing`, url `My%20Thing`. ➕ it is exactly the title. ➖ the url is ugly, and `page.My Thing` is not valid JS.
- **C. Spaces in the id, `-` in the url.** ➕ a nice url. ➖ a space and a `_` both turn into `-`, so the url can't be mapped back to the id.

**Leaning A.** A line may still say `#My Thing`; it is cleaned the same way before the lookup. A random id is used only when there is no title, or when `_2` would look wrong.

description: Where the page system is going, and the next steps.

add.title: The target: any Item can have a page
add.text:
Data is Items; a url opens any Item as a page.

```
Item      data, saved as lines
 └ List   page.items, page.content
Page      an Item + a url
```

- **A player is an Item, not a Page.** Opening its url draws a page around it.
- **Each item is saved where it fits:** a line in page.jsonl, its own file, or its own folder. One live copy per file.
- **One url reaches any item:** `/live/x/thing`.
- **One library of generic parts**, made live only where a page needs it.

add.title: Next steps, in order
add.text:
Five small merges, cheapest first.

1. **page.items lands** (in review now): an item in its own file, drawn and tailed live, opened at `/live/item-test/thing`.
2. **Tidy up:** move `TaskState.js` to core/Task, delete the old `parts/` alias files. *About 45 min.*
3. **One import:** a `core/core.js` entry file. *About 20 min.*
4. **Generic parts:** the Live\* cards become plain parts; a type name is its class name (`LiveCode`, not `live-code`).
5. **Decide the five questions below**, then build the one url scheme.

add.title: Five open questions
add.text:
Not decided yet; each one leans one way. [In full, with pros and cons](/live/plan/questions/).

1. **Item vs Page:** any Item can be opened as a page.
2. **One url:** short, searched in order: folder, then file, then the page's items.
3. **Trailing slash:** a file name + `/` draws it (`readme.md/`).
4. **Ids and urls:** `_` in ids, `-` in urls.
5. **Default id:** passed id, else file name, else the title as `my_thing`.
